title: u10.2! TONS OF BUFFS!
content:
u10.2!

This is probably the patch with the most buffs in all of TEKO. I also took the opportunity to fix some bugs. I'll be keeping an eye on feedback and will continue making the necessary adjustments.


Pocket Changes

Clarification: in the tweaks where there are 5 numbers separated by "/", it's a value for each difficulty, from D0 to D4.


🔵 Hacker Pocket

I've noticed that, generally speaking, the play size isn't as broken as it seems. This is a problem, because Hacker Pocket bases its entire advantage exactly on that feature. So, to compensate for having -1 max mana and +1 play size not being enough, I've added another effect; I also buffed its stats quite a bit so it can scale better in the early game.

  • NEW: all played chips will retrigger.
  • Draw size: 7 / 7 / 7 / 7 / 7 ⇒ 8 / 8 / 7 / 7 / 7.
  • Initial money: $10 / $10 / $10 / $10 / $10 ⇒ $12 / $14 / $16 / $16 / $16.
  • Score goal: -9% / -6% / 0% / +6% / +8% ⇒ -22% / -20% / -17% / -17% / -17%.
  • Overkill: -6% / -3% / 0% / +5% / +8% ⇒ -15% / -12% / -8% / -8% / -8%.
🟢 Outlaw Pocket

One of the most consistent and control-heavy pockets, despite being quite simple to play and having several advantages due to its fixed max mana, it was still suffering artificially, purely because of the numbers. So, it deserved a small stat buff, especially to overkill, which was punishing players a lot for trying to take advantage of the special combo mechanics.

  • Initial money: $4 / $3 / $2 / $2 / $9 ⇒ $16 / $13 / $11 / $11 / $11.
  • Score goal: -9% / -6% / 0% / +6% / +8% ⇒ -9% / -7% / -4% / -4% / -2%.
  • Overkill: -6% / -3% / 0% / +3% / +5% ⇒ -15% / -12% / -10% / -9% / -8%.
🟢 Linen Pocket

Unlike other pockets, it doesn't seem that dangerous. But, at the same time, it doesn't seem that broken either... unless you force the strategy that makes it unique, but achieving that requires a lot of money. The awful early game didn't let you remove cards or pivot to other strategies, making it a miserable pocket to play.

  • Initial money: $4 / $3 / $2 / $2 / $9 ⇒ $16 / $14 / $14 / $12 / $16.
  • Score goal: -9% / -6% / 0% / +6% / +8% ⇒ -14% / -10% / -8% / -6% / 0%.
🔴 Forbidden Pocket

The only pocket where you could consistently play without thinking and win anyway. It will now suffocate troll players more.

  • Initial money: $4 / $3 / $2 / $2 / $9 ⇒ $6 / $5 / $4 / $3 / $2.
  • Score goal: +4% / +8% / +10% / +12% / +15% ⇒ +12% / +16% / +20% / +24% / +30%.
  • Overkill: +8% / +10% / +12% / +14% / +16% ⇒ +8% / +13% / +16% / +20% / +25%.
🟢 Carpet Pocket

This was the most impossible pocket in the entire game. Literally, from D1 the chances of winning were 0%. I did a very aggressive buff. It's clear that the most important stat in the game is mana, and even though having infinite play size is broken, it doesn't replace the fact that players only get one chance per round to reach the score goal.

  • Discards: 4 / 4 / 3 / 3 / 3 ⇒ 5 / 5 / 4 / 4 / 4.
  • Initial money: $2 / $1 / $1 / $1 / $4 ⇒ $30 / $25 / $20 / $20 / $20.
  • Score goal: -5% / -2% / +2% / +9% / +12% ⇒ -30% / -25% / -20% / -20% / -20%.
  • Overkill: +1% / +2% / +3% / +7% / +11% ⇒ -40% / -35% / -30% / -30% / -25%.
🔵 Elite Pocket

Justice has been served! Not only was it one of the most boring pockets, but it was also hard to win with. It will now be more complex, yes, it will have more ways to break the game, but at the same time it will scale more aggressively to compensate for the new mechanic.

  • NEW: when entering the shop, each card has a 20% chance to become Sinister.
  • NEW: you can sell Sinister cards for $5 (fixed price).
  • +$1 sell value to all cards ⇒ +$2.
  • Initial money: $1 / $1 / $1 / $1 / $3 ⇒ $5 / $4 / $3 / $3 / $3.
  • Earn $1 for every saved money: $4 / $4 / $5 / $5 / $5 ⇒ $7 / $7 / $8 / $8 / $9.
  • Max interest earnings: $9 / $8 / $7 / $7 / $6 ⇒ $7 / $6 / $5 / $4 / $3.
  • Overkill: -6% / -3% / 0% / +5% / +8% ⇒ 0% / +2% / +4% / +8% / +12%.
🟢 Void Pocket

I thought this would be the hardest new pocket, and it turned out it wasn't. Still, the money penalty was too huge, preventing players from shining in the early game. And the huge advantage of unlimited overkill earnings can't always be exploited, so I reverted a mechanic that nerfed it.

  • Now it gives $1 for every 10% overkill, not every 15%.
  • Initial money: $0 / $0 / $0 / $0 / $0 ⇒ $18 / $16 / $14 / $12 / $10.
  • Score goal: +8% / +14% / +20% / +30% / +36% ⇒ +6% / +10% / +15% / +22% / +30%.
🟢 Cookie Pocket

I can't believe I'm doing this. Specifically for Hyper and Cookie pockets, I tried not to touch the values too much, because I thought they were already broken. Turns out this last one is very weak, even though its mechanic is great.

  • Score goal: -5% / 0% / +4% / +12% / +12% ⇒ -9% / -5% / -2% / 0% / +1%.
  • Initial money: $1 / $2 / $2 / $2 / $4 ⇒ $10 / $10 / $12 / $14 / $16.
General Changes

🟢 Score Goal

The same thing was happening in all pockets and difficulties: it was very hard to advance because the score goal scaled faster than the players' builds.

  • Lowered the percentage scaling for all difficulties.
  • Lowered the penalty system rates for achieving strong builds.
🔴 Sinister Cards

Despite the general buffs, I've reasoned that this trait is too broken, so I've created a new penalty.

  • The score goal will increase by 0.8% for each Sinister card.
  • For the Elite Pocket it will be 1.5%.
🔴 Safe Combo Upgrade Pack

I had to penalize combo upgrades a bit without affecting players too much. The best way to achieve this is by taking away money.

  • If the selected combo is level 6 or higher, it will take an extra $1.
  • If the selected combo is level 12 or higher, it will take an extra $2.
  • If the selected combo is level 15 or higher, it will take an extra $3.
🔴 Forbidden Cards Spawn Rate

I'm sorry. Since I created new cards with this trait, their appearance is way too frequent, therefore, I've adjusted it. And it will continue to be nerfed when I release more forbidden cards.

  • Rates: 1% / 0.75% / 0.4% / 0.25% / 0.1% ⇒ 0.4% / 0.3% / 0.2% / 0.1% / 0.05%.
🟢 Lankvian Boss

The famous run-killer boss. It's the only boss adjustment in this patch; even so, I'll soon prepare a patch dedicated entirely to the game's "villains".

  • Score goal: +40% ⇒ +20%.
Bug Fixes
  • If you discard a Full Mansion and have more than 1 Betrayal card, they all now play the corresponding trigger animation.
  • Cheers card now stacks correctly if there is more than one.
  • In-game clarification: the 3 nullifier bosses (pdz/yeni/gasparov) DO NOT stop special combos.
  • Cheapskate now gives a free reroll if you replace a card by opening it from a pack.
  • Fixed cards that act on the last turn (1 mana), especially for Outlaw and Carpet pockets. Example: Final Sacrifice Card.
  • If the round before ending a run had an element that removed chips (for example, Mikello card), the particle effect that was left "pending" no longer appears when starting the next run.
  • Stamp block (consumable) no longer generates infinite consumables if Pixibar card is being used. Right now it will work like this: if the player already has all 3 consumable slots filled and uses Stamp block, Pixibar will obligatorily NOT work to restore Stamp block.
  • Fixed multiple bugs with the Damn Mouthwatering Alfajor Card. Many consumables that could be used on the play screen, like the printer or the colored juices, weren't stacking for the card.
  • Fixed hovering on consumable screens like Masquerade when the player has a lot of cards.
  • Fixed tooltips that should appear at the bottom showing up on the right when they touch the edge.

That's all.

As you can tell, I worked a lot on balance, especially on the pockets. I had actually never given them that much importance; in fact, I thought modifying the cards was much more worth it. And this time, I was on the verge of creating and reworking several cards again, but I stopped myself. Instead, I dedicated myself to designing a system to simulate thousands of runs at once, and I discovered new strategies. I understood that most of the cards that seem like trolls are situational, and modifying them could break the game further, so I decided not to act on that front. Instead, I noticed there were pockets that were already capable enough of winning, and others that weren't.

As soon as I made the very first change: reducing the Score Goal scaling, most difficulties in all pockets were winnable. But specifically, pockets like Carpet were very complicated, and a general buff wasn't enough; I had to target them specifically. And so I did. Abundant buffs for the worst pockets. And even a rework for Hacker and Elite, which deserved it because playing with them was a headache.

Hard is not the same as impossible; really, the only impossible one was Carpet. In fact, a player managed to win with Hacker D4 before the buffs.

I've created 3 player archetypes for my simulator:

- Pro: plays optimally, efficiently, measures overkill, knows which cards are the best, uses all resources like the blenders.
- Noob: plays straightforwardly, mindlessly, without building an economy with interest, wastes their money, does a lot of overkill.
- Average: plays a bit more conservatively than the Noob but doesn't quite get as meticulous as the Pro; they make mistakes, don't make perfect plays, and fail to follow the meta strictly.

Lacking real feedback, I created my own machine capable of testing everything in hours instead of years. It practically saved TEKO's development.

And the goal was simple. For D0 to be winnable for anyone, even having noobs hovering around a 20% win rate. For average players to maintain a good win rate but have it drop in D4, where the Pros will shine, having a 50% win rate across all pockets on the highest difficulty.

Yes, I aimed for a 50% win rate. That's a lot compared to the 15-30% (or even less in some pockets) from before. The idea is that the best players can even go on win streaks.

What I've learned from TEKO is that it goes beyond the typical builds I had in mind. The possibilities are endless even though there's a meta. I even understood again why I created certain "troll" cards back then, which I was thinking of buffing today because I didn't understand why they existed. Everything definitely has a reason.

Today, more than ever, I am very aware of the game's balance, and much more so of the meta. At first, I was distressed knowing most of the game's secrets, but then my confidence and passion for numbers were reinforced. I feel much more in the loop and I've come up with dozens of different ideas to try in my builds. I've gone back to playing TEKO, and after several months of barely playing, I won a D4 pocket again.

I'm very proud of this new patch. My idea for several months now has been to leave the game in a playable state so new players don't have such a hard time, and veterans can get hooked again.

Right now, I think TEKO is a completely solid game. I can finally say this with certainty.

I hope you can understand the effort and love behind this project, and as you can tell, I was on top of it for 2 straight years without stopping work. I want to enter a stable period.

New content? There can be, clearly. NEVER doubt that. I have hundreds of ideas that can become a reality. But, I want to be PATIENT! Even if I have free time, I prefer to wait for now. I'll continue designing new content, but I won't implement it into the game just yet. When the time is right, I will. The idea is to not lose the balance.

Thanks for everything.

title: Special announcement...
content:
I'm going to be honest with you.

There are some things in TEKO that haven't been fully tested.

This is mainly because I've put all my efforts into finishing the content and fixing bugs, leaving balance testing aside because I assumed feedback would be enough.

Right now TEKO is unbalanced, but in a negative way: the win rate, even for the best players, is very low.

And no, this doesn't mean I haven't played at all; in fact, lately I did play a lot, to the point of exhaustion, but seriously, my limits as a human are weak. A single person can't test a ROGUELIKE game this much. After so many runs, there comes a point where I start playing the exact same way, without enthusiasm and without wanting to think, and I become inefficient. This is directly harmful.

First and foremost, I want to apologize for this. I did make it hard on purpose, because at the time I wrote several conditions to make the game tough. I knew it was hard, but I didn't know it was almost impossible. I did that unknowingly. I never meant to take it to this extreme.

I'm sorry; I should've taken more time, and I shouldn't have released so many pockets without testing them as much as possible.

But along with these apologies comes good news, of course, otherwise it wouldn't make sense. I hate it when someone apologizes but doesn't change for the better. I'm ready to take my work to the next level.

I got obsessed with the numbers and the math behind TEKO. A few days ago, I started playing dozens of runs, over 15 a day. I started seeing beyond just the card "meta". Knowing that this is pure logic and probability, aside from generating infinite theories on how to play better, I developed a machine learning simulator. This simulator seems to be working well for now, and it's yielding consistent results. I spent 30 hours developing it, and it shows a lot of promise. The main reason I need this is so I can simulate thousands of runs at once, train thousands of bots per hour, and learn so much more about my own game. And in fact, I've already drawn several conclusions, but as the weeks go by, I'll learn more about TEKO's objective balance and its mathematical secrets. From what I can see, if the simulations for certain pockets fail to advance rounds, it's clearly impossible to win. And if it's too easy to win, I'll notice that too. Often, it's not the cards' fault; it's the pockets' fault. And... the Score Goal's fault.

Well, one of the things I need to perfect is the Score Goal scaling formula per round. I've already been tweaking several values, and I've noticed a massive increase in the win rate with just a few changes. Few, but substantial. I know now: the worst part of the game is the scaling.

I'm going to go further, and aside from having a basic simulation, I need to generate more data, like resource utilization (tubes, pillbox, etc.), the economy, the amount of efficient overkill, etc. The ideal scenario is understanding my game's consistency. Yes, it's a roguelike, it has RNG, and it can't be "100% solved", but I need to understand it deeply to enhance the best parts and allow top players to win on the hardest difficulties and even have long win streaks.

Consider yourselves warned: TEKO is very hard, and my current recommendation is to play pockets on low difficulties (from D0 to D2). Remember, for now TEKO is our laboratory and we are experimenting. But soon, it will be an efficient machine.

Now that I've finished all the initial content and there are already so many cards and pockets, my only goal is to leave TEKO in a playable and WINNABLE state. I promise I'll put in all my effort; seriously, these past few days I've only been thinking about this. I fell in love with my own game's numbers, finally, and I plan to push past the abstract barrier to objectify things.

Thank you all for bearing with this long process. I swear you will see results at some point. It's very likely that in less than a month I'll have made several highly important changes, and it will be reflected in everyone's win rate.

title: TEKO Database!
content:
u10.1
We now have a public database!

From now on, there'll be an option in the settings to enable/disable data sending. This data is anonymous and sending it doesn't consume extra resources. It helps a ton with game balance, so I recommend leaving it enabled. What does it do? It sends run info: which pocket was played, on what difficulty, which cards were used, etc.

And all that data will be reflected on the Wiki.

Specifically, here you can see: Runs Stats / Cards Stats / Pockets Stats!

Obviously, right after patches launch, nothing will show up yet. The database updates automatically once a day (though for the first few days I'll update it manually so it fills up with data), so expect it to work properly after multiple players play several runs following each major patch (for example, the new 10.0 patch has only been out for 1 day, so data probably won't be properly reflected until 2–3 days from now).

The tables will only reset once we move to the next major patch; meaning, in this case, all data will accumulate until 11.0.

I spent 20 hours working on this. I hope you like it, find it useful, and that it helps me improve the game. I haven't collected data in almost a year. Now I'm back at it.

Finally, the new update 10 is here.

I hope you can enjoy these 5 new pockets with unique mechanics and 5 forbidden cards that are heavily unbalanced to make each run more interesting. I've also added the 10 corresponding new achievements; TEKO is only 18 achievements away from reaching 100.

To unlock the pockets, you won't have to win with other pockets; you'll have to complete specific achievements. To unlock the cards, you'll need to beat the last level of each pocket.

Right now, the pockets might be a bit unbalanced. I'll be adjusting them as patches go by.

There are 2 things I dedicated to a follower: the Hyper Pocket and the Hyperpop Queen Card were made in honor of the first person who got hooked on TEKO for dozens of hours: Zoe. She has been around since the beginning, and her favorite strategy was always filling pink tubes, so I gave her unique interactions related to her build preferences. I really like commemorating the people who have always been there; I have a good memory.

Soon I'll make a couple more items dedicated to other followers of the game who have been there since the beginning. And in the distant future, I plan to make another batch of new dedicated content.

Also, with the creation of the "Dev Apology" card, I obviously took the opportunity to keep reinforcing the MEME of the "hexagons" that are actually octagons. I know it's silly, but it's never going to change. It's already like that, and it will stay like that forever. And I find it really funny because at first, I did it by accident, since I saw that the octagonal shape looked much better and then I forgot to check how many sides it had, and then that chip's sprite went down in history permanently.

This is a patch full of beautiful things. I really enjoyed making it. I hope someone can win a D4 run with the Void Pocket; please, if anyone is capable of it, send me a screenshot of the build on Discord. I need to see it XD.

And, pls, report any bugs or imbalances.

title: New content!
content:
I'm back. With a little surprise in my hands...

I'm preparing the following content for u10.0:

- 5 new pockets!

- 5 new forbidden cards!

I really wanted to make an update with little content but meaningful, meaning that each new element adds many hours of gameplay or something new. In this case, I've opted to add more raw game hours with new pockets, and fill out the roster of forbidden cards, since until now there were only 3. And, you know: my goal is for all types of content to be complete. Previously I had already made updates for mods, stickers, chips. And even many new cards, but never specifically forbidden cards. So it was about time.

I have hundreds of ideas, and my plan is to release new content gradually. Try to make updates frequent again. Few new things in each update, but making it feel like I'm advancing fast. That's right. The only thing that stresses me out about development is when I make massive updates. I prefer to make short expansions, the progress is more noticeable.

Honestly, if I still had practice I could make this update in just 1 week without complications. But 2 months ago I lost my development rhythm. And I'm going to have to pick everything back up. It's not relearning, it's simply reviewing it and getting used to it again. Down at the bottom at the end of the post, I'll explain why this hiatus happened.

First I wanted to answer some frequently asked questions.

When is Early Access going to end?

Previously it was planned for the end of the year, but if I keep coming up with things and have a lot of work, I think it will be in the first half of 2027. I have several goals. In general, I'd like TEKO to keep gaining visibility through each update, and when I feel ready, EA will end, and I'll keep making expansions anyway. The idea is that the end of EA means the end of all structural changes, QoL, etc. Balance and content patches will never stop.

What does "u10.0" mean? Games usually reach "1.0" when they finish EA!

"U" stands for "Update". Each significant content patch is the advancement of a whole number, whereas QoL or balance patches are decimals. This way it's much better understood how the game has advanced. Almost all devs use the version number in a more generic way and it ends up not being understood, simply making "1.0" mean that the game has finished developing in EA. I count each big patch. Until now there have been 9 content updates since TEKO is at u9.0. This way we can gauge how much it has grown. In the future it will be more impressive.

And the discounts?

I consider TEKO's price to be fine. And besides, it has never increased. Therefore, I have decided (at least for now) not to offer large sales. I've only put -10% during festivals. In the future or on special occasions maybe I can offer bigger discounts, but I doubt that will happen soon. In general, my idea is to keep the price like this forever, even with regional prices, and not offer a discount for now. In a few years maybe this will change, but I want you to know that in the short term, my plan is this. I say this so you don't wait for discounts to buy the game.

What awaits us?

As soon as u10.0 appears, I'll resume the previous rhythm, but much faster. I hope to at least be able to release a big patch every month. If I'm lucky, I could even release a content update every 2 weeks. But first I need to get into inertia, and for that prior preparation is required. I don't know how long until the new patch launches, but as soon as it happens, take it as a sign that Daddy Talio is back in the game.

Now for real...

I have to talk about something serious.

I didn't want to draw attention, nor put it in the title of the post, nor make a circus around this, because clearly it's not the right thing to do, besides, actually if I wanted to I could not tell anyone, but I prefer to do it so you can get to know me a little better. Nor am I looking for victimization. I simply have to tell it so you can have another point of view on game development. Remember, every personal thing I tell about myself is related to TEKO. Anything that happens to me influences my games, since all these works are handicrafts made personally by me alone. That is to say, games are my life, therefore, they reflect a part of it.

I have autism and ADHD. After 2 intense months I have finished the diagnosis. I always knew I was like an alien among humans, but I had never suspected all this due to my ignorance. In fact, just a few months ago I discovered what these 2 conditions truly were, and by entering the rabbit hole I ended up at a professional getting tested. It was very stressful doing all this. Many things I thought were strange now have a logical explanation. In part I feel much better, and less guilty or weird. But the diagnosis process was very long and disconnected me from everything I like, since I tend to have inflexible routines, and going to a psychological center every week pulled me away from my perfectly scheduled daily activities. As soon as the process started, my whole life got disordered. Lately I've been suffering quite a bit of mental and physical pain, and it's because of the annoyance of doing something new. When I go through changes, I suffer. And I fell into a burnout. Nothing was the same anymore and I didn't feel like doing anything, not even at all. I was exhausted. Just a few days ago I finished the diagnosis and almost instantly I started resuming my activities that I liked so much and I have much more physical and mental energy. I still feel weird and I know a lot of work awaits me, in fact, this is just the beginning. I feel like I've been reborn. I'm another person. I don't regret going to a professional because from now on I can only improve. I want to keep working on my projects, especially on TEKO. Now more than ever I feel united to my favorite game. And, while I work, I'm going to have an important introspective process, to finally start therapy after. But first I have to sort out a lot of things inside my head! Because I'm confused. I feel in a moment of total discovery, and I don't plan to stop digging into my mind until I understand myself completely. Without a doubt, I've always been an analytical person, but now without ignorance I feel my limits have expanded. I need to reflect on this, talk to my family, start the process on my own, and then, with professional help, find objective solutions to everything. I love being the way I am, honestly, without my behavioral patterns it would have been impossible to do all this, since this is part of me, my arts, my creations, my stories, my desire to play video games, I love all this and I'll never stop loving it. But there are very bad things, like high stress, masking, anxiety, burnouts, extreme inflexibility, in conjunction with an ADHD that keeps getting in my way, it's hard for me to start activities, finish them, sometimes I want to change activity, I enter an extreme circle of thoughts. When I hyperfocus I'm an efficient machine, when I don't, I'm useless. Everything that happens to me can improve, and even indirectly improve the quality of my games. For example, what does what happens outside my house have to do with TEKO? Well, if I were a person capable of carrying out a bit of unmasking, I would probably return home with more energy, therefore, more capacity to work on TEKO. It's just an example, we can apply this to everything. That's why I say my games are a reflection of my reality.

I have a huge internal world that I've built since childhood. Pixi (TEKO's protagonist) is an alien bird that I created at age 6, in my first comic. I feel an enormous attachment to my games because everything you can see is the product of my mind's imagination. That's why things like art I take very seriously and they have that personal and distinctive aesthetic of mine. Next year when TEKO leaves EA, I'll start writing the novels of my world, which will be totally related to my game. I plan to invest a lot of time and money in all this. For me, all this that arises from my creativity is the most important thing in my life. These characters and what happens to them is much more serious than other things in real life. I have the need to show the world this entire universe housed in my brain. I'll keep doing it through all these artistic mediums. Never doubt it. Thanks for reading me!

title: TEKO Demo is back!
content:
TEKO Demo is finally here!

The free version returns with more content than ever.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4069700/TEKO_Demo/The new version contains tons of extra content, so those who try the demo can satisfy all their curiosity, and finally decide if they want to get the full version. I estimate that, to complete all its content, you need more than 30 hours of playtime. Well, in fact, it's possible to play endlessly since the gameplay loop is complete and there are no limitations. It features 42 achievements/unlockables (THIS IS HALF OF THE FULL GAME IN ITS CURRENT VERSION!), but the player can keep playing even if they have 100% progress if they want to.

Finally, the Demo is high quality and represents the real game. I love it. Plus, you don't just play one Pocket. The Jean Pocket is available in difficulties 0, 1, and 2; and it also lets you try out the Hacker and Warlock pockets, two of the best pockets in all of TEKO.

Honestly, I hope this leads to a larger audience discovering the game. If you like the current demo and would like to support me, you could review it; that's very important for the visibility of indie games.

Besides having in-game unlockables, it also has Steam achievements. And, the demo's progress synchronizes with the full game, so players who transition from one version to the other will keep their perks!

If TEKO gets unlocked by Steam, I promise to do a lot of things. I'm so hyped. 'Unlocking' means when the game reaches a certain amount of sales, enough for many perks like showing up on profile showcases, unlocking trading cards, removing the 100-achievement limit, unlocking profile badges, emotes, etc. This is incredibly important for a game to gain more popularity because it shows up in more places on Steam. I swear that, if we manage to do it, I'll release a new extreme content pack. I was planning to add at least 50 new cards and 15 new pockets to the full version. How much is this? Like 1500 extra hours of playtime. Plus, I could finally create the trading cards, which I've been wanting to do for a long time. Well, you'll see. I hope things go well and we reach the most important milestone so far. When we get there, you'll be surprised, 100% guaranteed. Don't forget it.

There's a follower who has been a Patreon member for over 12 months now. In fact, he's the only one. Thank you so much Franmax3000 for supporting me for an entire year! I'll dedicate some subtle, subliminal content to you, a hidden element in TEKO, for being the first user to support me this much <3.

Steam had my Demo blocked for several days (the system prevented it from being published on the store page) and it also happened right as the weekend started (the platform's support doesn't work on these days), so it was a frustrating week. In the process, maybe some weird things happened. If you see any bug, let me know. I check everything.

I'm proud to be so communicative with the community. I never stay quiet, and that's why you get to know everything I'm doing, and thanks to the posts, people know I'm active. Without a doubt, I'll keep it up.

title: The end is near.
content:
I think TEKO is finished.

I'll quickly explain the latest patch (u9.1.1) and then I'll tell you some important things.

- Improved the run save system: previously, when closing the game suddenly or exiting from the settings to the main menu, the run would save in any intermediate state no matter what, so sometimes when trying to return to the run, the game would get frozen between states. I actually shouldn't have ever put those 2 save points because the game was already saving well enough, and it was what caused the biggest issues. The run now saves correctly when the player is on the Shop Filter screen (the new feature). It no longer saves in the shop when using items even if you're not in the shop (this error has been happening since it became possible to use consumables on the play screen). You should now be able to exit to the Main Menu in the middle of chip plays (I had previously forbidden this due to bugs). According to my fixes, it only has to save when you draw chips for the first time, once per round. In the shop, it should save whenever items are used or bought.

I finally understand why many indie games take months to make a system like this. Some games even leave EA and still haven't finished their Save System. Well, in my case, it's guaranteed that it should work at least 90%. Please, if you notice specific things that don't save correctly, let me know. I promise to fix everything I'm aware of. I tested it on my own and didn't see any bugs! remember that the game gets little feedback, there are only a few of us playing TEKO.

- Now, if the player has a lot of chips, on the chip display on the play screen, the text will shrink so it fits properly.

- When entering the Codex, Preview Boss, Settings, or Pocket selector (all menu screens), previously on Discord/Steam's rich presence it appeared as if the player was in a run instead of "Main Menu". This has now been fixed.

- The tutorial screen for new players was changed to match the current aesthetics.

That's all.

Since I started creating my third game, I've come up with things for TEKO. This is great, it seems my imagination is back at its peak. I feel really good and I'd like to keep it that way. Maybe, by putting energy into another project, I've stopped feeling so much pressure with TEKO. Or maybe it's a mental effect generated because TEKO's development is finally coming to an end. Just to clarify, this doesn't mean I won't make content expansions. Finishing the technical development is one thing, and the amount of gameplay is another. TEKO aims to be infinite in that regard.

In a few months, I'll probably need testers for the 3D RPG I'm creating. So you can join the Discord. I'll announce and give important information there in the future.

I'd like to improve my first game (Almohadin). It's finished, but there are things I never polished, like the interface. And I'd also like to make a system for it to be played entirely with a keyboard or controller, because I've noticed it's easy to implement in such a simple game. Thanks to my TEKO knowledge, I'm capable of improving my first game. Maybe I'll do it at some point. I'll never close the doors on continuing to develop any of my projects. This is something I love doing. And I still love AEFTB just as much as the first day. I have a sense of attachment to every game I make. It's very likely that in a few months we might see a beautiful, huge update that will leave everyone surprised. I don't promise it 100%, but I want you to know it's in my plans to continue with all of this.

I made an important post on Patreon (it's FREE), giving some conclusions on TEKO's balance, in case you're curious and want to see some interesting data.

A few weeks ago, I was lucky enough to be able to take a vacation. It seems that made my project improve. I remember that at the beginning of the vacation, I got really stressed because I overloaded myself with tasks. I think this was inevitable. I took my time, meaning I didn't rush as much, but I still got tired. This is normal. It's something you have to go through. I don't want people to think I'm sick of the project just because I got exhausted for a few days! for as long as I can remember, I know that when I'm about to finish a long job, the exact same thing happens to me. And well, what happened to me a few weeks ago was a sign that TEKO was about to be completed. Now I feel a great sense of joy. I feel liberated. In fact, that's why the RPG idea came up, because I was able to clear my mind.

The truth is, it doesn't matter what happens anymore. I finished it. I did what I promised. TEKO is a fact, it's real. I'm satisfied now, I finished it just the way I imagined it from the beginning (even better). I don't regret anything, these 2 years of development, all the effort it took, the frustration. Today I can say I overcame it. I want that, even if only 5 people play my little game, the few who have seen it, to be witnesses of what consistency can achieve, and for it to serve as an example for their own lives; in the end, that's what all this I achieved is about: inspiring others. If I could do it, you can too. Don't give up, and even if you have obligations and boring things in life, never forget what makes you happy and truly entertains you, and never abandon your inner child. Finally, I did what I promised Pixi many years ago. If my old friend were real, he would be proud.

title: Things are changing
content:
The Artwork:

I didn't think it was that big of a deal, enough to receive several messages from different people criticizing my latest artwork. Still, being self-critical, there was room for improvement. And so, I did it.

Briefly: at first, I had a very colorful artwork with too many elements, very "rough" because the lines were ultra-thick, but with a lot of personality. Then, I changed it to an overly simple cover, with just a single character and nothing else. Both images had things that could be improved, so I combined the two: keep it simple, but at the same time incorporate something to properly fill the rest of the canvas, while representing the game's genre somehow.

Currently, the cover shows the 2 most important characters in TEKO: Pixi / Yeni. Yes, they are the ones that appear the most on the cards; then there's Talio and Gasparov. If you pay attention, you'll notice there are many sprites that relate to each other (BECAUSE THEY ARE THE SAME CHARACTER DRAWN IN A DIFFERENT WAY!). Also, I drew cards. The problem with my game: it's very complicated to represent "chips" and "cards" because they don't work like in other games. What did I do? I represented them more classically as if they were from a normal deck. And I took the opportunity to place one of the most important elements of the game (The Crystal Tower), creating a combination between Poker and Tarot cards.

In the post where I announced the new visual changes, when I said the new elements represented the game better, I was specifically referring to the new trailer and screenshots. However, the game's cover has to be simple, and it isn't always obligated to represent it faithfully. Even so, I wanted to change things, so I decided to reuse the old background (the wooden table, the purple tapestry, and the green rug) and the yellow color from the old text. And I redrew Pixi in a realistic way!

Yes, I'm so sorry, Pixi. You scare people, everyone prejudges you. You know what? Unfortunately, with the previous design, people were afraid to get into my game because he seemed like a deformed and poorly drawn creature. In my opinion, he was always cool. But I had to update him to draw more attention and make it clear that he's an ALIEN BIRD! Before, he looked like something else and people could get confused.

And no, I wasn't going to waste the illustration of Yeni. So, I put them both together. Besides, Yeni is holding an Ultracolor Chip, subtly representing one of the most important elements in TEKO.

I think this is the definitive work. Usually, when I'm very sure of something, I don't listen to others. But, when I finished the previous artwork I still had doubts. That, added to the fact that some people wrote to me (respectfully) about what they thought of my "aaaah goon waifu bait cover", made me rethink things and generate new ideas. In my opinion, things are much better now. Even so, I'll never discredit my own work. So far TEKO has had 4 covers, and I don't hate any of the 4. They're all different, and each one has an EXPLANATION and a MEANING. Until you understand this, it's impossible to know why I did things the way I did.

Anyway, I'm proud of having taken the time for this. I got a bit stressed out, not from drawing, but from coming up with new ideas and the concept I wanted to capture. Now the elements of poker + 2D fantasy should be understood.

I'm never going to underestimate people who share their opinions about my stuff. Although, art is subjective. Even so, I want you to know I always read the comments. I understand people, and I try to find a middle ground between what I want and what others want. Obviously, I'm always the priority. But if there's room for change and people want a change, if I think it's a good idea, I'll do it. I'll always be open to opinions, especially if they are made respectfully like they have been so far.

The Demo:

I want more people to wishlist my game. At the same time, I want more people to play TEKO. I'm going to prepare a new DEMO completely faithful to the latest version, which will also HAVE THE FULL GAMEPLAY LOOP and a lot of content. Yes, the pockets and cards will be limited, but it'll have so much to offer. And this will lead to a lot of people getting interested in the full version. Until now I was holding back, because I wanted to improve the official version. Soon, when I finish polishing the game 100%, I'll launch the demo, and this will help a lot. I'm excited and really looking forward to it.

My next game:

I'm making an RPG. Yes. I don't know what's going to happen, I'm not promising anything. I just want to show you a bit of what I'm doing. I'm taking my time, trying to enjoy and think things through, imagining what my ideal game for this subgenre would look like. I have a lot of plans and you'll see more stuff (plus I created a YouTube series to document everything from scratch). I hope this new path turns out great. This isn't going to replace any of my other simultaneous projects, just clarifying just in case, I'm doing it in my free time. TEKO's development is not affected by the RPG.

NEW! Shop Filter Feature. Now, after beating the round 13 boss, the player will be able to choose which items they don't want to show up on sale in the shop for the rest of the run. This feature has also been added as an achievement.

Along with the Shop Filter, you can also revert the pre-bans made to cards!

Both in the Shop Filter and the Codex, the 'Current' text for the cards values should now be visible. I think this wasn't happening before; it has been fixed. There was a small issue calling the respective lines.

Added a new button to reset the card ban selection in the codex.

2 Steam achievements (pre-ban & boss preview features) have been fixed and can now be earned retroactively.

Fixed two errors when changing profiles: (1) a white border would appear on the sides of the screen, it was a screen manager bug. (2) On the next run, shapeless chips would appear instead of the normal ones.

Now mod texts can stack in the tooltip (if you have more than 1 mod of the same type, it will show, for example, 'x2' instead of repeating the name and its description twice).

The text on the button to buy card slots has been made smaller (in its Spanish version, it didn't fit well before).

title: Good news for TEKO
content:
I'm happy to announce that I've finally revamped some elements of the Steam Store Page for TEKO. I've wanted to do this for a long time, and I finally managed to do it. I changed everything, from the trailer to the cover image and the description. Now everything looks prettier and better represents the game in its current state.

I have a lot of plans for the game. I'll make some of them a reality, others will depend on the motivation people give me. If I see that more and more people like the game, I plan to put in more effort. During all these years of development, I NEVER relied on feedback or public approval, but now more than ever, I think making extreme new changes will only be worth it if I get a larger player base.

Some of the changes I have in mind for upcoming versions are:

  • Control: I'd like the game to support any kind of input. Currently, you can only play with a mouse, but in the future, I'd like it to be 100% playable with: just a keyboard, PlayStation/Xbox controllers, Steam Deck, etc.

  • Translation: I'll be completely honest, I don't have money, much less to pay for localizations. My plan is the following: find people who want to collaborate for free on localization, then run all the game's text through an automatic translator, and have the volunteers just fix the mistakes instead of doing every single line one by one; I'd just need quality and coherence control. This is the best way for me to do things. But I absolutely need native speakers for each language. I'm not going to rely solely on a machine to translate everything; I mandatorily want at least one person to manually review each language. If at any point someone is interested in helping me out for free, you can let me know, and we can implement a new translation. We already have the English and Spanish text complete, now I want to expand specifically to ALL LANGUAGES, no matter which one.

  • Shop item ban mechanic: this is similar to the pre-ban system, but instead of before the run, it's during it. And it'll only affect items on sale, not other elements like packs. It will serve to block items from showing up when you reroll. It'll be incredibly important for the game's balance.

  • Balance: I have some things planned for balance, like changing the rarity of cards, or customizing the difficulty more for each Pocket.

  • Content: I want to add extreme mechanics that change the whole game, especially with Pockets. I have too many good ideas, and when I say too many I mean that implementing all this content would mean expanding TEKO's gameplay by more than 1000 extra hours. It is, without exaggerating, insane. Not just the pocket ideas (the game's core mechanic), but cards too. I can start working on this whenever I want, since everything is written down and planned, but I can't jump into the void and start a new streak of new content without the backing of a solid community. Therefore, I prefer to take a break from development to focus my efforts on increasing the amount of people playing TEKO, so I can take big steps later. I'M WILLING TO SUPPORT THE GAME FOR MONTHS OR YEARS. Never doubt that.

I just added 2 new achievements to Steam (the 2 new unlocked mechanics, added in version 9.0).

I just updated the whole website, especially the Wiki, I recommend you go in and see what's there, plus I improved the tierlist. I had a lot of fun doing this.

Don't forget to join the Discord server, you can ask me any questions or give any kind of feedback or idea.

Don't forget that you can support me on Patreon. I'll soon upload some surprise content there, even some FREE POSTS! (yes, you can follow me for free).

Please, consider leaving a Review on TEKO's Store Page, it would help me a lot. The game's visibility truly depends on this.
